brief: A week of central bank decisions delivered a deliberate, measured tightening signal, while risk-asset volatility tied to AI overtook energy as the main driver of global duration. In the US, Fed Chair Warsh's schedule-change announcement read as dovish, but GS expects an every-other-meeting hike pace to continue (baseline December, risk of March) and closes its receive-10s SOFR fly for a long-5s UST fly, partly on Treasury's expected steady refunding sizes. The BoC hiked 25bp with a hawkish tone, but GS fades the cumulative hike pricing as excessive and recommends CAD front-end flatteners. The ECB looks on track for a December hike with a vol-dampening tone, favoring EUR 5y outperformance. The BoE is expected to deliver its first hike next week, but the bar for further hawkish repricing is high, favoring long GBP vs EUR front-end vol. The UK Budget cleared a near-term hurdle on supply but left longer-term Gilt issuance higher, favoring 10y underperformance. The BoJ shifted to a December hike partly to defend the Yen, while safe-haven flows support JGB richening. The RBNZ surprised with a hold, favoring NZD steepeners, while the RBA's expected hike next week is seen as the cycle's last, prompting GS to close its AUD flattener.
